templates.band: Recorded by this app’s developer on {approved_on} from {agency}’s announcement of {date_published_verbatim}: {kind_label}. Why: {kind_phrase} — {kind_basis} This app shows this until {until_day}: {until_basis}. The regulation text is unchanged.
templates.band_typed: Recorded from the owner’s own reading, by this app’s developer on {approved_on}, of {agency}’s announcement of {date_published_verbatim}: {kind_label}. Why: {typed_basis} This app shows this until {until_day}: {until_basis}. The regulation text is unchanged.
templates.band_ended: No longer shown from {expired_on}: this status {expiry_reason}.
templates.band_lifted: No longer shown from {lifted_on}: {lift_label}, in {agency}’s announcement of {lifted_by_date_published_verbatim}: “{lifted_by_title_verbatim}”.
templates.announced_line: Shown from {since_day}: the day the agency’s own words name for the change, or, where this app read no such day, the California day the agency’s feed dated the announcement. When the change takes effect is in the agency’s own words, quoted here.
templates.announced_line_unquoted: Shown from {since_day}: the day the agency’s own words name for the change, or, where this app read no such day, the California day the agency’s feed dated the announcement. When the change takes effect is in the agency’s own words, in the announcement linked here.
templates.renewal_line: Recorded again by this app’s developer on {approved_on} from the same announcement, because this app’s own 180-day cap on the earlier status was near. Its end is counted from {renewal_day}, not from the announced-on day.
templates.planner_line: Recorded by this app’s developer on {approved_on} from {agency}’s announcement of {date_published_verbatim}: {kind_label}. This app shows this until {until_day}: {until_basis}.
templates.clause_line: This rule is named in a status recorded by this app’s developer on {approved_on} from {agency}’s announcement of {date_published_verbatim}.
templates.read_at_line: This app last checked its in-season statuses against their end dates on {read_at}.

until_basis_text.explicit_end_in_announcement: the last day the agency itself printed in its announcement
until_basis_text.printed_season_end: the last day of the season this record prints
until_basis_text.apps_own_cap: this app’s own 180-day cap: the agency’s quoted words state no end date
until_basis_text.apps_own_cap_unquoted: this app’s own 180-day cap: this app read no end date (the agency’s quoted words were withheld)

expiry_reason_text.reached_agency_end: reached the last day the agency itself printed for it
expiry_reason_text.reached_printed_season_end: reached the last day of the season this record prints
expiry_reason_text.reached_apps_own_cap: reached this app’s own 180-day cap; this app read no end date from the agency for it
expiry_reason_text.lifted_by_announcement: was lifted by a later announcement from the agency
expiry_reason_text.renewed: was recorded again by this app’s developer from the same announcement, with a new end date
expiry_reason_text.record_retired: was recorded against a record, or a rule of it, that this app’s regulation data no longer carries

hotline_gap: Some in-season changes, reopenings included, are announced by recorded telephone message. This app reads what the department publishes on its website and does not hear those recordings, so a status here can outlast a change announced only by telephone.
no_value_moved: No regulation text in this app changed because of these statuses. Each one is this app’s developer’s reading of an agency’s announcement, printed beside the text it concerns.
scope_rule: A status recorded from an announcement alone withdraws “Open now” from the record it names and says nothing else. Only a closure whose rules this app’s developer named, one by one or as every rule the record prints, says those rules are closed, and only those rules. A restriction never says a rule is closed: it withdraws “Open now” from the rules it names, or from the whole record.
day_rule: A status is shown from the calendar day the agency’s own words name for the change: a date after “as of”, “effective”, “beginning”, “starting”, “from” or “on and after”, or after “at” a time of day “on”. That whole day counts, whatever time of day the words print. Where this app read no such day in them, it is shown from the California calendar day the agency’s feed dated the announcement. Where they name two different days, this app records no status from that announcement.
until_rule: A status ends after the last day the agency printed in a quoted sentence that reads “through” or “until” a date, that day included. A quoted sentence that reads “for the rest of the calendar year” or “through the end of” a year ends the status after December 31 of the year named, or of the year it was announced where none is named. Where this app read no such sentence, it ends after the earlier of the season end this record prints and this app’s own 180-day cap. A status recorded again from the same announcement counts both from its renewal day instead of its announced-on day.
expiry_rule: Nothing leaves this file without a stated reason. A status that has ended stays here, with the day it ended and why, for thirty days afterwards.
approval_rule: Nothing is recorded here until this app’s developer answers, in writing, one proposal that quotes the agency’s announcement. Each answer is kept with its date.
read_at_rule: `read_at` is the day this app last evaluated its table of statuses against the calendar. It is a fact about a past evaluation and it is not a claim about how often this app evaluates anything.

rows: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

CDFW’s 2026-09-11 release is titled “Lower Klamath River Quota Met” and says meeting the quota “triggers the closure of the adult Chinook salmon fishery on the main stem of the Klamath River”. The headline carries no closure word, so it is declared by name. The same release says the lower river “will remain open to the harvest of jack (2-year-old) Chinook salmon”, which is why a status read from it alone is closed in part.
The fishery at the mouth of the Klamath closed Wednesday, Sept. 2 and will remain closed to all fishing for the rest of the calendar year.
